source.title: A new adaptive gradient method with gradient decomposition
source.authors: Zhou Shao; Hang Zhou; Tong Lin

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with SGD-family methods on held-out performance using different optimizer methods and benchmark tasks; it does not test random-label memorization or the original claim’s full set of conditions.
record.gate_note: Own optimizer-comparison results on natural-label classification and language-model tasks bear on V4. Claims about results from cited papers, convergence theory, and values visible only in plots are not extracted as results. DecGD c-sweep is reported descriptively but its plotted values are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The paper's new DecGD and AEGD results compare adaptive optimization with SGDM on held-out image and language performance, bearing on V4. Most Adam-family and SGDM values are imported from AdaBelief, so their relative rankings are not independent findings of this study. DecGD outperforming Adam alone does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase broadly captures the authors' position: they present DecGD as combining rapid convergence with generalization better than SGDM and competitive with leading adaptive methods. Their claim of broad hyperparameter robustness exceeds the reported c sweep; Appendix F.3 leaves learning-rate and AMS robustness for future work. Their CIFAR-10 ResNet-34 prose also contradicts Table 1: DecGD accuracy is 95.37%, below AdaBelief's 95.44%.
record.recipe_differences: Tests optimizer comparisons on standard image and language tasks with reported test accuracy or perplexity; compares DecGD and representative optimizers rather than testing the claim's limited-tuning Adam-versus-SGD setup directly. CIFAR optimizer results partly reuse values reported in AdaBelief.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and model affect the relative ranking; LSTM perplexity differs by depth. The paper reports robustness to c choices for ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, but values are figure-only.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Several optimizer comparison values are reused from AdaBelief rather than independently run in this paper. The paper reports no results for AMSGrad and AEGD on Penn Treebank due to poor performance and tuning effort. Plot-based curves have no extractable exact values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No required version-specific numeric table results were left out. Figure-only training curves and the ResNet-18 c sensitivity curves were not turned into numeric rows because exact values are not stated.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for interpolation.
Matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and the role of local connectivity.

An independent Adam-versus-SGDM replication; tuning only learning rates and schedules for Adam-family methods, since beta parameters are also searched; a controlled comparison of limited versus broader tuning; Adam-to-SGD switching; decoupled-weight-decay recovery; and comparable training performance.
Batch-size effects and recipes for overcoming large-batch penalties.
Dropout ablations and their interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus removing random examples.

missing.what: New AEGD versus imported SGDM test accuracies: CIFAR-10 ResNet-34, 93.25% versus 94.64%; DenseNet-121, 92.97% versus 94.50%; CIFAR-100 ResNet-34, 75.18% versus 76.06%; DenseNet-121, 76.72% versus 77.59%. These provide adaptive-versus-SGDM comparisons omitted from the record.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. Imported optimizer results may serve as attributed baselines for new DecGD or AEGD measurements, but cannot supply independent Adam-versus-SGDM evidence. DecGD's favorable results qualify the scope of adaptive-optimizer disadvantage; they do not refute the version's 'often' formulation. No uncertainty estimates establish the reliability of the reported differences.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization after fitting random labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Limited-tuning adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons on cited image and language benchmarks outside this paper's experiments; broader tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, and the other stated qualifications.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptation to large batches.
Dropout versus no dropout and interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.
